title: Physical RIFT Workbridge GUI quarantine — second read-only investigation and comparison

scope.gameClient: physical RIFT Live x64 on host Windows 11

executiveFinding.confirmedPresentBlocker: Persistent Workbridge desktop GUI-turn lock plus linked quarantine sidecar from an uncertain physical-RIFT screenshot on 2026-11-02; no verified manual reconciliation/archival of that incident.
executiveFinding.preciseUnderlyingScreenshotFailure: unknown; no original request-specific success/error receipt found, and the classification covers multiple failure modes
executiveFinding.basisForHistoricalProcessGone: Fresh Win32_OperatingSystem.LastBootUpTime is 2026-11-05T15:26:47.500Z, after the 2026-11-02 incident; no original process can have survived continuously through this boot. This does not prove historical screenshot success or historical process-tree settlement.
executiveFinding.runtimeSafetyFixStatus: Deployed through authorized WB-001 at 2026-11-05T20:17:50.5294819Z; ten installed dist files independently SHA256-equal sealed payload. Old quarantine intentionally preserved.
executiveFinding.generalPurposeGameInputInterface: No supported general-purpose physical-RIFT keyboard/mouse MCP tool currently registered; this is a separate gap from the quarantine, and a /reloadui attempt was not made.
executiveFinding.mostPlausibleImmediateTrigger: An inner Microsoft WinApp CLI call hitting its default 15-second timeout is consistent with the 15.614-second lock-to-quarantine interval, but this is inference only; original suberror and deployed November 2 payload were not recovered.
executiveFinding.recoveryProgress: Subsequent separate approved Workbridge workflow has already prestaged and independently verified byte-exact backups of both Nov2 artifacts; originals remain active. A handle-bound no-replace archival mover has not been implemented/tested or used; release remains pending.

mechanism.caller: src/desktop-registration.ts withDesktopCaptureTurn: atomic open(lockPath,'wx') maps EEXIST to UI_TURN_BUSY; unsettled failures preserve lock and write matching sidecar.
mechanism.runner: src/desktop-cli-runner.ts createDesktopPrototypeInvoker runs child Node wrapper; timeout, force-kill, nonzero child exit or invalid output can yield DESKTOP_TREE_UNSETTLED because wrapper termination does not certify grandchildren.
mechanism.timestampConstraint: Quarantine sidecar created approximately 15.6s after lock; this is NOT evidence of reaching the default 45s timeout, because callers can supply a shorter timeout and other errors can trigger the same classification.
mechanism.noAutomaticRelease: The design lacks time-based expiry for uncertain operations; original lease is preserved across game and Workbridge restarts and OS boot.
mechanism.innerWinApp: scripts/desktop-ui.mjs runWinapp default timeout is 15000ms. On timeout it kills its direct child and waits for close, without independently certifying all descendants.
mechanism.screenshotCallSequence: scripts/desktop-capture.mjs performs version check, windows listing, UI inspect, second listing, and screenshot serially; these do not override the inner default timeout.
mechanism.outerDefault: The outer Node wrapper defaults to 45000ms in src/desktop-cli-runner.ts; src/desktop-capture-tool.ts does not supply an override. The 15.614-second incident is not evidence of the outer 45-second deadline.
mechanism.lostSubcause: src/desktop-cli-runner.ts collapses a nonzero Node-wrapper exit into DESKTOP_TREE_UNSETTLED before parsing its structured error output; DesktopPrototypeError.interruptedBy is not stored in the quarantine record. Persisted sidecar omits original WINAPP_* code, child PID, exit status, stage and timeout setting.

proved: The quarantine is Workbridge-owned and tied to one November 2 physical-RIFT screenshot request.
Original lock and sidecar remain linked, SHA-identical and unmodified in the second inspection.
Original owner no longer runs; the PC booted after incident.
Guarded source/runtime has now been deployed, but historical quarantine remains.
The four registered desktop MCP tools are windows, inspect, capture_window, capture_vmware_host; no general-purpose game keyboard action tool exists in this registered interface.
